newsitem.title: GERMANY: Douglas says 1997 likely to be difficult.
newsitem.headline: Douglas says 1997 likely to be difficult.

text.p: German speciality retailer Douglas Holding AG said on Wednesday its net income rose two percent in 1996 to 105.6 million marks but said it expected 1997 to be a difficult year in general for retailers.

But Douglas, which operates cosmetics and jewellery stores, said it was prepared to deal with any downturn and forecast sales at about 4.5 billion marks, up from the three percent gain in 1996 to 4.3 billion marks.
Shares in Douglas slumped on the news, falling 90 pfennigs to 57.70 marks in late bourse trade while the broader 30-share DAX index was up more than 1.60 percent at 3,393.58 points.

Douglas chief executive Joern Kreke declined to predict at the group's annual news conference whether earnings in 1997 would top 1996 levels, saying it would depend on consumer confidence in the economy and prospects for higher spending.

The company said it would propose an unchanged dividend of 1.40 marks per share -- the same it has paid since 1993 when its profit from ordinary activities was 227.3 million marks and above the 1996 level of 201.9 million marks.
"We have had better results than we did last year," Kreke said in putting doubt on whether Douglas would raise its dividend payout in 1997.

Douglas, which operates 1,821 stores in Europe, said sales at its perfume shops rose seven percent to 1.67 billion marks, while jewellery sales fell to 853 million marks from 866 million marks in 1995.
The group finished 1996 with 17,388 employees, 615 more than at the end of 1995.
